_comment: The closed vocabularies that cross the TypeScript <-> Rust process boundary.
This file is the source. `node vocabulary/generate.mjs` emits crates/drift-engine/src/vocabulary.rs
and packages/core/src/vocabulary.ts from it; `--check` verifies the committed output matches.
Both generated files are committed so `cargo build` and `tsc` need no generator step.
Before this existed the two sides were hand-maintained mirrors. Measured drift at the time of
writing: check-repo's fact_kind_from_str knew 30 of 36 fact kinds, get_repo_map's role enum knew
17 of 21 file roles, get_conventions' kind enum knew 9 of 23 convention kinds, and the scan/
semantic capability namespaces were disjoint by construction, which made semantic_coverage.decision
the literal string "refuse" on every repo. Nothing compared any of these lists.
A member added here becomes a variant on both sides. On the Rust side the generated enums have
exhaustive as_wire/from_wire matches, and the hand-written dispatch matches over them, so an
unhandled member is a compile error rather than a silent drop through a `_ => None` arm.
`wire` is the string on the wire. Rust variant names are derived by PascalCasing it, which is
checked by the generator - a member whose derived name would collide is a generator error.

fact_kind.doc: Every fact kind the engine can emit. Declared to the CLI in the `scan_started` handshake so an incompatible pairing is refused before any fact is ingested.

graph_node_kind.doc: Node kinds in the fact graph. Part of the `scan_started` handshake alongside fact kinds: before W5 the engine emitted these as bare strings, so a kind the CLI did not know produced a Zod enum failure and exit 1 rather than the exit-3 refusal the handshake exists to give.

graph_edge_kind.doc: Edge kinds in the fact graph. Same handshake as node kinds.

file_role.doc: Roles a file can be detected as. Crosses the boundary inside `file_role_detected` facts, `file_role` graph nodes, convention matchers (`applies_to_file_roles`) and the MCP get_repo_map filter.

route_flavor.doc: CV-2: what kind of caller a route serves. Conditions convention scope (`applies_to_route_flavors`) and carried across the boundary in `route_flavor_detected` facts.

parser_gap_kind.doc: Why a region of the repo could not be understood. Derived CLI-side from engine diagnostic codes, and referenced by the semantic capability contracts, whose parser_gap_kinds must be members of this list.

doc: D-P3a: every convention kind, and where each one dispatches.
The 23 kinds were evaluated by three mechanisms - a literal-match chain in check_command.rs, the
is_phase6_security_convention predicate beside it, and a separate chain in the CLI's run-check.ts -
with three more accepted by the schema and implemented nowhere. No single place listed all of them,
so a 24th kind with no evaluator would have been caught by nothing: `check` returns a clean pass for
a contract that enforces nothing.
`dispatch` is now that place. The generated Rust ConventionDispatch is matched exhaustively by the
engine, so a new kind that names no target does not compile.
dispatch values:
engine_direct - a dedicated arm in crates/drift-engine/src/check_command.rs
engine_phase6 - the shared Phase 6 evaluator in the same file
cli           - an arm in packages/cli/src/check/run-check.ts
none          - accepted by the schema, implemented by neither (UNIMPLEMENTED_CONVENTION_KINDS)
`proposable` marks the kinds candidate inference can propose. It is exactly the set the engine's
candidate payload used to declare in its own hand-written enum.
`security_contract` marks the kinds that carry a security boundary proof. Three lists claimed
to be this set and two of them agreed: SecurityContractKindSchema (13) and
EngineSecurityContractKindSchema (13) against EXPERIMENTAL_SECURITY_CONVENTION_KINDS (12),
which omitted api_route_forbids_secret_exposure - the flag that keeps every security kind
behind --experimental-security, missing the one kind whose whole subject is secrets.
`requires_engine_source` marks the kinds whose engine evaluator re-reads the route file from
disk instead of working from the facts on the wire. All twelve security kinds do. Without
`repo_root` - which the wire protocol declares Option<String> - every one of them silently
produced nothing, and `check` reported a clean pass. See D-F1 in check_command.rs.
D-S1: the one capability namespace.
These ids are what may appear in EngineCapabilityStats (certified/required/missing),
EngineCompleteness.{required,missing}_capabilities, and therefore in ScanCapabilityReport and the
semantic coverage contract built from it.
There used to be two namespaces with zero string overlap BY CONSTRUCTION: the engine emitted bare
names (`graph_stream`, `route_detection`) and BUILTIN_SEMANTIC_CAPABILITIES declared eight ids of
the form `ts.<name>.v1`. A hand-written translation table in packages/query/src/semantic-coverage.ts
was supposed to bridge them and named four capabilities the engine has never emitted
(`data_operations`, `data_operation_facts`, `fact_graph`, `route_flow`).
The bare namespace won because it is the one on the wire: nine of the eleven sites that PRODUCE a
capability id already emitted bare names (both Rust capability_stats call sites, repo_completeness,
check_command's fourteen security labels, candidate_command, run-check.ts, convention-candidates.ts,
factgraph's two completeness entries, the TypeScript fallback's degraded list). The `ts.*.v1`
namespace appeared in exactly three places - the contract list itself and the two
DEFAULT_PREFLIGHT_CAPABILITIES references - none of which produced wire data.
`engine_certified` marks the members crates/drift-engine/src/protocol.rs::certified_capabilities()
reports. `security` marks the members security_capabilities() reports (D-P3b).
